name: GILBERT SYNDROME (UGT1A1 GENOTYPING)
interpretation:
The Mutational profiling of the genetic information obtained from patient has revealed that patient carries the UGT1A1*28 allele in homozygous form. This could explain patient’s hyperbilirubinemia (if present) as being caused by Gilbert syndrome due to defective production of the enzyme responsible for bilirubin clearance.

RECOMMENDATIONS:

  • Clinical correlation is recommended.
  • Familial first degree relative testing for this allele may inform risk of pathogenicity in family members.
  • Please note this sample is analyzed for presumed Gilbert syndrome evaluation, please contact lab for re-analysis in case pharmacogenetic analysis is required.

TEST INFORMATION:

Gilbert’s syndrome, a chronic non-hemolytic unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia, is caused by a reduction in the activity of hepatic bilirubin UDP-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT1A1). This reduction has been shown to be due to a polymorphism in the promoter region of the UGT1A1 gene. The presence of seven thymine adenine (TA) repeats reduces the efficiency of transcription of the UGT1A1 gene. Other two mutations at Codon 71 and 486 also screened in this assay. These two mutations reduced UGT1A1 enzyme activity.

METHODOLOGY:

Bi-directional DNA sequencing was carried out using 3500/3730XL Genetic Analyzer Applied Biosystems (ABI) for the three common polymorphism present in UGT1A1 gene. The data were analyzed using CodonCode Aligner v5.0.2 (CodonCode Corporation, Centerville, MA, USA) and/or Mutation Surveyor v5.0 (Softgenetics, State College, PA, USA).

LIMITATIONS:

  • Clinical diagnosis and therapy should not be based solely on this assay. The results should be considered in conjunction with clinical information, physical evaluation, and additional diagnostic tests.
  •  In rare cases because of allele dropout, heterozygosity may be reported as homozygosity.
  • This test is designed to detect mutations in the above-mentioned regions only. Sequences surrounding the regions of interest are analyzed but not reported.
  • Results have been confirmed by bidirectional sequencing, with the error rate of the Taq polymerase for base incorporation being 1 in 6000 bases.
